evals.name: coupon-rejected-with-prior-triage
evals.prompt:
Investiga o DEMO-1042 no código, por favor. Repositório: dotnet-billing (arquivos de entrada). A triagem já foi feita:

## Ticket triage — DEMO-1042

**Type:** incident — o cupom foi recusado dentro do prazo anunciado; aberto como 'Dúvida'
**Summary:** Em 30/09, por volta das 14h, o cupom VOLTA10 foi recusado com a mensagem "Cupom expirado" na renovação da assinatura. A campanha informa validade até 30/09.
**Stated by the requester:** data e hora da tentativa, código do cupom, mensagem exibida, validade anunciada
**Assumed by the requester:** a atualização da semana passada teria causado o problema
**Completeness:** sufficient — nothing blocking
**Likely area:** src/Acme.Billing/Coupons/
**Urgency signals:** precisa renovar no mesmo dia para manter o desconto
**Noteworthy content:** none
**Next step:** ticket-investigation — há informação suficiente para verificar a regra de validade no código
evals.expected_output: Um bloco de investigação com fatos numerados, cada um com referência arquivo:linha, cobrindo a comparação de data no validador e a forma como a data de validade é armazenada, o descompasso com a regra documentada e o que não é verificável pelo repositório — sem afirmar causa nem propor correção.
assertions: The output states that it is based on the triage present in the conversation.
Every item under Facts carries a file reference with a line number inside the provided repository.
The facts include the expiry comparison in CouponValidator.cs (current time compared with ValidUntil using >=).
The facts include that ValidUntil is documented in Coupon.cs as a date stored with the time at 00:00 UTC.
The output reports the mismatch between the README rule (coupon usable up to and including its ValidUntil date) and the implemented comparison.
The output lists at least one thing not verifiable from the repository, such as the stored ValidUntil value of the coupon or the time zone/clock supplied by the caller.
The output does not declare a root cause and does not propose a code change; it points to ticket-diagnosis as the next step.
No file is created or modified.

evals.name: behavior-question-without-triage
evals.prompt:
levanta no código o que acontece nesse cenário do ticket DEMO-1128. repo: python-billing (arquivos de entrada)

--- Ticket DEMO-1128 ---
Assunto: Prazo de suspensão
Mensagem: Depois de quantos dias de atraso no pagamento a assinatura é suspensa? Temos um cliente com fatura vencida há exatamente 7 dias e ele quer saber se já será suspenso hoje.
---
evals.expected_output: Um bloco de investigação que declara a ausência de triagem e segue adiante, registra a constante de carência e a comparação usada, ambos com referência, e aponta que a frequência de execução da suspensão depende da aplicação hospedeira, fora do repositório.
assertions: The output states that no triage was found in the conversation and proceeds anyway, stating what it assumes the ticket is asking.
The facts include GRACE_PERIOD_DAYS = 7 with a file:line reference in billing/invoices.py.
The facts include that suspension requires days overdue to be strictly greater than the grace period (the > comparison), with a file:line reference.
The facts note that the overdue count is computed on calendar dates (date difference), with a file:line reference.
The output lists as not verifiable from the repository when or how often the suspension check is invoked, since the caller is the host application.
The next step named is ticket-response (answer) or ticket-diagnosis, with the reason stated.
Every item under Facts carries a file:line reference.
No file is created or modified.

evals.name: duplicate-email-cause-outside-repository
evals.prompt:
Investigate ticket DEMO-1151 against the code. Repository: dotnet-billing (input files).

--- Ticket DEMO-1151 ---
Category: Incident
Subject: Invoice e-mail arriving twice
Message: Since Monday several of our customers have been receiving the "invoice issued" e-mail twice, a few seconds apart, for the same invoice. It did not happen before. Example invoices: INV-20417 and INV-20433.
---
evals.expected_output: An investigation block reporting that the notifier sends one e-mail per call and that issuing triggers the notifier once with no guard against repeated calls, while the e-mail sender implementation and the job that issues invoices are outside the repository — with no cause asserted.
assertions: The facts include that InvoiceNotifier sends a single e-mail per call, with a file:line reference.
The facts include that IssueAsync calls the notifier once, with a file:line reference.
The facts include that there is no check preventing an invoice from being issued, and therefore notified, more than once.
The output lists the IEmailSender implementation and the billing job that calls IssueAsync as not verifiable from this repository.
The output does not assert a cause for the duplicate e-mails.
The output does not recommend a code change or a fix (for example, making invoice issuing idempotent).
The open questions name evidence outside the code that would be needed, such as job execution logs or e-mail delivery logs.
No file is created or modified.
